transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12
Start: 16:15 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood Solutions), Liam O'Connor (Cobalt Procurement), Priya Kapoor (Cobalt Legal), Diego Morales (Cobalt InfoSec), Sara Li (Cobalt Finance)

Summary:
Quick procurement/contract intake—customer has an MSA redline, needs pricing approver sign-off, and clarity on KMS/BYOK and data residency. Focus on whether hosted API with VPC/private plane is acceptable vs dedicated. Action: Redwood to send an MSA friendly bundle and schedule SE deep dive.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA priorities, SLA expectations, KMS/BYOK, VPC/private control plane, pricing approver path, pilot commit levels, audit logs retention.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Patel: All right, thanks everyone for joining. uh, afternoon for some of you, morning for others. we'll, we'll kick off. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. we also have Maya and Evan on the line. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hi, Liam here. Procurement. I'm the one who takes the paperwork and tries not to get too excited by redlines.
[00:17] Priya Kapoor: Priya, legal counsel. I'll run through the MSA and DPA items.
[00:20] Diego Morales: Diego, InfoSec. I'll focus on encryption, KMS, and network controls.
[00:24] Sara Li: Sara, finance, i'll handle pricing approval and billing questions.
[00:28] Maya Chen: hi, Maya, SE at Redwood - I'll be the technical lead for the deep dive.
[00:32] Jordan Patel: Cool. High level agenda: priya's redline walk, diego's security checklist, sara's pricing path, then we confirm next steps.

[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Okay. So we shared the MSA redline earlier this morning. big ones are: liability cap adjustments, deletion obligations in the DPA, and subprocessors list. we also want clarity on data residency — some of our PII can't leave eu.
[01:05] Jordan Patel: Understood. When you say data residency, is this a hard requirement for all workloads or specific product types?
[01:11] Priya Kapoor: It's primarily PHI-adjacent metadata for certain clinical workflows. so yes, for those tenants we need EU only processing and at-rest residency in eu region.
[01:22] Maya Chen: We can support model pinning to region, and for Private deployments we can run the control plane in VPC in customer region. the hosted API can be restricted by regional routing but we do need to confirm subprocessors - some telemetry goes to our EU logging cluster — can ensure it's in region.
[01:41] Diego Morales: On KMS — we prefer BYOK with HSM-backed keys. what does redwood support?
[01:48] Evan Park: We support customer-managed keys via an integrated KMS workflow. currently we've got GCP/ AWS KMS, and an HSM-backed option for private deployments. There might be a short lead time on HSM provisioning, but it's supported.
[02:03] Diego Morales: Okay can you also confirm that logs are encrypted at rest and segregated per customer?
[02:09] Maya Chen: Logs are encrypted at rest, and we maintain per-customer log partitions — though in the hosted tier we still have shared control plane components. dedicated pools and private deployments give stronger isolation.
[02:22] Liam O'Connor: On the procurement side we need to understand the billing cadence and if a pilot commit will convert to an annual commitment automatically or not — Sara is concerned about auto-renew traps.
[02:34] Sara Li: Right, we need explicit terms. we don't want a pilot to auto-upgrade without finance sign-off. what's your default?
[02:40] Jordan Patel: By default, pilots are month-to-month and do not auto-convert. Any reserved capacity or Dedicated commit is explicit and requires sign-off. We'll add a clause to the MSA to that effect.
[02:51] Priya Kapoor: Liability cap — your standard is 3x fees or a fixed amount? we usually push for clearer carve-outs for breach related to regulatory fines.
[03:01] Jordan Patel: Our standard is 3x fees or $5m, whichever is greater, but we can discuss carve-outs for regulatory penalties — those are typically negotiated on enterprise deals.
[03:11] Diego Morales: Back to security, how are search and indexing handled? is any data used for model training? we need assurance on no training on customer data.
[03:21] Maya Chen: Redwood's policy for customer-managed deployments is no training on customer data. For hosted API, we have an opt-out and enterprise plans include a guaranteed non-training clause in the DPA. Sometimes auto-ml analytics are done on anonymized aggregates for platform health, but we can add contractual language.
[03:39] Priya Kapoor: we'll need a DPA clause explicitly forbidding training, and a subprocessor list. Also deletion SLA: if a customer requests deletion we expect confirmation within 30 days, with forensic attestations for permanent deletion.
[03:54] Evan Park: We can commit to 30 days for standard deletion across hosted logs and caches; for backups there is a longer tombstone window but we can provide attestations. we'll detail timelines in the DPA.
[04:06] Liam O'Connor: We've got a couple of procurement nuances — we run a pricing approver committee, usually needs a 2-week window to review, and they ask for unit economics: per-token cost at estimated throughput. do you have sample TCO for a pilot vs dedicated pool?
[04:21] Jordan Patel: Yes, we'll share a simple TCO sheet: pilot (hosted) per-token price, and dedicated reserved monthly cost with expected throughput and latency targets. Also include quantization and batching guidance to reduce cost.
[04:33] Sara Li: For budget approval we need an explicit invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and cancellation penalties if any.
[04:39] Jordan Patel: We'll propose monthly billing for pilots, and monthly or quarterly for reserved capacity. cancellation terms will be explicitly listed.

[05:00] Diego Morales: Do you have SOC2 and ISO reports available? And pen test results?
[05:07] Evan Park: Yes, SOC2 Type II summary and ISO 27001 cert are available under NDA. We also have a pen-test summary and remediation timeline. we'll include those in the security pack.
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: For the MSA redline, some of our legal team has non-standard indemnities — we'll flag them but prefer to start with your standard and iterate.
[05:27] Jordan Patel: Sounds good. we'll send a 'redline-friendly' bundle: clean MSA, marked-up MSA showing suggested compromises, DPA, SOC2 + ISO artifacts, HSM/KMS integration docs, and an initial TCO pack.

[05:38] Maya Chen: One technical caveat to surface: if you want guaranteed sub-20ms tail latency for production, dedicated pool plus continuous KV cache and prefix caching is required; hosted pilot can hit reasonable latencies but not SLA-backed tails.
[05:54] Diego Morales: We'll need an SLA for uptime and incident response times. abnormal compliance incidents need an escalation path and forensic timeline.
[06:03] Jordan Patel: Our enterprise SLA includes uptime commitment, incident response RTO/RPO and a named escalation path; we'll include a sample SLA in the bundle.

[06:18] Liam O'Connor: timeline question — we want procurement sign-off by end of month. is that realistic?
[06:23] Jordan Patel: If we get your redline priorities this week and we send the bundle by 4/14, coupled with your pricing approver committee review two weeks, it's tight but doable.

[06:35] Priya Kapoor: we'll prioritize DPA items: data residency, no-training, deletion SLA. Others can be deprioritized for now.
[06:42] Sara Li: I'll need the TCO by 4/16 to bring to our approvers. Also note: we may ask for a 60-day payment term, that's part of our standard.
[06:52] Jordan Patel: Noted. we'll include payment term options and note standard terms vs custom 60-day.

[07:03] Evan Park: quick note for the SE deep dive: bring network diagrams, expected per-tenant throughput, typical prompt/response sizes, and whether you'll want BYOK or Redwood-managed KMS.
[07:12] Maya Chen: we'll also prepare a latency/cost tradeoff doc with examples of batching, request sizing, and quantization recommendations.

[07:22] Priya Kapoor: Any competitors influencing this decision? we've run a pilot with another vendor that wanted broader data access, which was a red flag.
[07:30] Jordan Patel: Nothing we can't address — we outlined non-training guarantees and region pinning. we'll clarify subprocessors list.

[07:38] Liam O'Connor: final logistics: who's the main point for procurement? it's me. For legal it's Priya, security Diego, finance Sara. Jordan for Redwood?
[07:46] Jordan Patel: Yep, me. I'll be your AE lead; Maya for technical. Evan will handle security artifacts.

[07:53] --- Recap / Next steps ---
[07:55] Jordan Patel: Recap: Redwood to send by 2026-04-14 — clean MSA, redline-friendly MSA, DPA with deletion timelines, SOC2 + ISO artifacts, HSM/KMS integration doc, SLA sample, and TCO pricing sheet. Customer to provide prioritized DPA redlines by 2026-04-16. Customer to confirm pricing approver calendar and preferred invoice terms by 2026-04-16. Schedule SE technical deep dive week of 2026-04-20.
[08:20] Priya Kapoor: that works. we'll aim to get the DPA priorities to you by the due date.
[08:24] Sara Li: I'll review TCO and get back with any billing constraints.
[08:27] Diego Morales: I'll send a short list of network and KMS requirements to Evan.
[08:31] Jordan Patel: Great, thanks everyone. End call.

[08:34] (end of recording)
